newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.

text.p: The Lebanese pound continued its rise against the dollar in a quiet market in the week ended on Friday, and dealers said Lebanese banks' plans to cut the prime lending rate had been expected and did not affect the market.

The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band during the week to 1,543.5-1,553 pounds per dollar from 1,544-1,553 and the dollar traded at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said.
Nabil Abou Jaoude, Treasurer and Chief Dealer at Banque Libanaise pour Le Commerce, said trade was restricted to a tight range of up to 30 piastres at the bid end of the intervention band.
Most of the offer of dollars was taken up by commercial banks. There were few orders for dollars in the last few days, probably commercial orders, but they were met, he said.
"The trend is still the same, there are offers of dollars and demand for pounds in a quiet market," Abou Jaoude said.

"The banks' plans to cut the Lebanese pound prime lending rate to 16 percent from 18 percent did not affect the market, because it was expected and investors see the trend of interest rates decreasing," he added.

The Lebanese Banks Association said on Thursday that it planned to cut the pound prime rate soon in line with reduced yields on Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills and to boost lending in the local currency.
